title: Tensor and composition coherence of ringed-topos projection maps
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be morphisms of ringed topoi presented by sites small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their canonical derived adjunctions, tensor pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and direct-image composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. For $h=f,g,gf$, define
$$\pi_{h,E,Q}:Rh_*E\otimes^L Q\longrightarrow Rh_*(E\otimes^L Lh^*Q)$$
as the adjunct of $\varepsilon_{h,E}\otimes1$ after the pullback tensor comparison, where $\varepsilon_h$ is the canonical counit. These projection maps are natural in both arguments, are the identity for $h=\mathrm{id}$, and obey the following two coherence identities, with all associators and canonical pullback/direct-image comparisons understood:
$$\pi_{f,E,Q\otimes^L T}=\pi_{f,E\otimes^L Lf^*Q,T}\circ(\pi_{f,E,Q}\otimes1_T)$$
for $E\in D(X)$, $Q,T\in D(Y)$, and
$$\pi_{gf,E,Q}=Rg_*(\pi_{f,E,Lg^*Q})\circ\pi_{g,Rf_*E,Q}$$
for $E\in D(X)$, $Q\in D(Z)$. In the first identity the target is $Rf_*(E\otimes^L Lf^*Q\otimes^L Lf^*T)$; in the second it is $Rg_*Rf_*(E\otimes^L Lf^*Lg^*Q)$.

In particular let $i:X\to W$ and $p:W\to X$ be morphisms of ringed topoi with a specified isomorphism $pi\cong\mathrm{id}_X$. Under $Rp_*Ri_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $Li^*Lp^*\cong\mathrm{id}$, the composite
$$ M\otimes^L V\cong M\otimes^L Rp_*Ri_*V\xrightarrow{\pi_p}Rp_*(Lp^*M\otimes^L Ri_*V)\xrightarrow{Rp_*\pi_i}Rp_*Ri_*(M\otimes^L V)\cong M\otimes^L V$$
is the identity for arbitrary $M,V\in D(X)$; the displayed projection arrows use tensor symmetry to order factors as written. No projection isomorphism or boundedness assumption is needed for these equalities.

proof.text:
Put $P_h=Lh^*$, $R_h=Rh_*$, $t_h:P_h(A\otimes B)\cong P_hA\otimes P_hB$, suppressing the superscript $L$ on tensors. Use [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] for its associator, symmetry, identity and adjunction-compatible composition comparisons. Let $b_h(A,E)$ denote the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(A,R_hE)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P_hA,E)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], the defining property of $\pi$ is the equation
$$\varepsilon_{h,E\otimes P_hQ}\circ P_h(\pi_{h,E,Q})=(\varepsilon_{h,E}\otimes1)\circ t_{h;R_hE,Q}.\tag{*}$$
The bijection makes this equation a uniqueness criterion for $\pi$. These constructions apply to arbitrary unbounded $E,Q$.

proof.text: For $a:E\to E'$ and $b:Q\to Q'$, transpose the two naturality composites. Naturality of the counit gives $a\varepsilon_{h,E}=\varepsilon_{h,E'}P_hR_h(a)$, and naturality of $t_h$ gives $t_hP_h(R_h(a)\otimes b)=(P_hR_h(a)\otimes P_h(b))t_h$. Hence both transposes are $(a\varepsilon_{h,E}\otimes P_h(b))t_h$. Injectivity of $b_h$ proves naturality in both variables. For $h=\mathrm{id}$ the comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] identify $P_h,R_h,t_h,\varepsilon_h$ with identities. Equation (*) then has right side $1$, and its unique adjunct is $1$.

proof.text:
Fix $f$, and abbreviate $P=P_f$, $R=R_f$, $t=t_f$, $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_f$. Identify parenthesizations by the associators. Set $B=E\otimes PQ$ and $C=B\otimes PT$. The transpose of the right side of the tensor identity is
$$\varepsilon_C P(\pi_{f,B,T})P(\pi_{f,E,Q}\otimes1_T)
=(\varepsilon_B\otimes1_{PT})t_{RB,T}P(\pi_{f,E,Q}\otimes1_T)
=((\varepsilon_B P\pi_{f,E,Q})\otimes1_{PT})t_{RE\otimes Q,T}
=(\varepsilon_E\otimes1_{PQ}\otimes1_{PT})(t_{RE,Q}\otimes1_{PT})t_{RE\otimes Q,T}.$$
The first and third equalities are (*); the second is naturality of $t$. The associativity coherence in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] identifies the last expression with
$$(1_E\otimes t_{Q,T})(\varepsilon_E\otimes1_{P(Q\otimes T)})t_{RE,Q\otimes T}.$$
This is the transpose of $R(1_E\otimes t_{Q,T})\pi_{f,E,Q\otimes T}$, by (*) and counit naturality. Injectivity of $b_f$ gives exactly the first identity, including the target comparison $R(1_E\otimes t_{Q,T})$.

For composition use the comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to write $P_{gf}=P_fP_g$, $R_{gf}=R_gR_f$, $t_{gf}=t_f\circ P_f(t_g)$ and $\varepsilon_{gf}=\varepsilon_f\circ P_f(\varepsilon_g)$. Put $V=E\otimes P_fP_gQ$. Transpose the proposed composite $R_g(\pi_{f,E,P_gQ})\pi_{g,R_fE,Q}$ first through $P_g\dashv R_g$. By counit naturality and (*) its transpose is
$$\pi_{f,E,P_gQ}\circ(\varepsilon_{g,R_fE}\otimes1_{P_gQ})\circ t_{g;R_gR_fE,Q}.$$
Transpose this through $P_f\dashv R_f$. By (*) and naturality of $t_f$, the result is
$$(\varepsilon_{f,E}\otimes1)\,t_{f;R_fE,P_gQ}\,P_f(\varepsilon_{g,R_fE}\otimes1)\,P_f(t_{g;R_gR_fE,Q})
=(\varepsilon_{f,E}P_f\varepsilon_{g,R_fE}\otimes1)\,t_{f;P_gR_gR_fE,P_gQ}\,P_f(t_{g;R_gR_fE,Q}).$$
The normalized counit and monoidal comparison equations identify this with $(\varepsilon_{gf,E}\otimes1)t_{gf;R_{gf}E,Q}$. It is the transpose of $\pi_{gf,E,Q}$ by (*). The composite Hom bijection in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] is injective, proving the second identity for the specified canonical comparisons.

For $i:X\to W$, $p:W\to X$, first use the order $V\otimes M$ for the source. Apply the composition identity just proved with $f=i$, $g=p$, $E=V$, $Q=M$:
$$R_p(\pi_{i,V,P_pM})\circ\pi_{p,R_iV,M}=\pi_{pi,V,M}.$$
The specified ringed isomorphism $pi\cong\mathrm{id}_X$ induces the monoidal and adjunction-compatible comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Substitution in (*) therefore identifies $\pi_{pi,V,M}$ with $\pi_{\mathrm{id},V,M}=1_{V\otimes M}$. To return to the displayed order in the statement, let $\beta$ denote tensor symmetry. The left-ordered projection is, by definition,
$$\widetilde\pi_{h,A,B}=R_h(\beta_{B,P_hA})\circ\pi_{h,B,A}\circ\beta_{A,R_hB}.$$
The displayed composite is thus $\beta_{V,M}\circ\pi_{pi,V,M}\circ\beta_{M,V}$. Naturality moves the inner symmetries across $R_p$ and $R_i$, and the two adjacent symmetries on $R_iV\otimes P_pM$ cancel; the final symmetry under $R_pR_i$ becomes $\beta_{V,M}$ under the comparisons. Since $\beta_{V,M}\beta_{M,V}=1$, this composite is $1_{M\otimes V}$. Only the proved identities and symmetry were used; no projection map was inverted.
